articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice for Week 5
articles.summary: Justin Boone gets those lineups in shape for Week 5 fantasy football.
articles.body:
Make any day feel like Game Day with the Burger King Game Day Menu. Before you take your first bite, get your lineup ready with this week's must-starts and sits.

Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 5 rankings .

Stafford's fantasy numbers have been a mixed bag in the opening month, with two weeks as a top-10 QB and two finishes outside the top 25. Fortunately, his next matchup has the makings for one of the best prime-time shootouts of the season.

The Rams will host the Bills on Monday Night Football, in a game tied for the highest projected point total on the week at 54.5.

Buffalo is allowing the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing passers, including a QB1 overall result to Drake Maye last week.

Drake Maye vs. Raiders – Speaking of Maye, he finally looked more like his 2025 self in Week 4. The most exciting outcome was his season-highs in carries (8) and rushing yards (54), which Mike Vrabel highlighted as a key to their victory. If Maye keeps it up, he'll return to high-end fantasy QB1 territory.

Jared Goff at Cardinals – Goff might not be at home for this one, but this is a dome game with a 54.5 projected point total against an Arizona defense that's giving up the fifth-most fantasy points to QBs.

With Rico Dowdle sitting out the last couple of games due to a toe injury, Warren has made the most of his increased workload. Despite not finding the end zone in either contest, he still racked up 302 scrimmage yards and six receptions on 44 touches during those two weeks.

Dowdle is practicing on a limited basis so far this week and may return to the lineup, but Warren remains a strong start either way after showcasing his potential recently.

The Colts are also the eighth-best matchup for fantasy RBs, which is by far his easiest opponent through the first five weeks. You can confidently start Warren once again whether Dowdle is active or not.

Bhayshul Tuten vs. Eagles (London) – Tuten was one of my recommended buys this week, since he's been so close to much bigger stat lines recently. He's RB16 on the year, topping 85 scrimmage yards in three of his four games and is coming off season-highs in usage. He also had two TDs called back due to penalties last week. He should see plenty of work with the Jags heavily favored over the banged-up Eagles.

Emanuel Wilson vs. 49ers – Wilson is coming off a 120-yard, two-touchdown effort and facing a 49ers defense that's let four different backs reach double-digit fantasy points against them in four weeks. Seattle also ran all over San Francisco in its matchups last season.

Braelon Allen vs. Browns – It's hard to judge the Jets offense based on their performance in Week 4, since the Bears completely controlled the game and time of possession. Even so, Allen finished with 16 touches, including all 14 of New York's rushing attempts. I like his chances against a Browns defense allowing 103.5 scrimmage yards per game to starting RBs this season.

Williams was highlighted as a start last week in this space and answered the call with six receptions and 102 yards on eight targets. Is it risky to go back to the well expecting another spike week from the volatile WR3? Yes, but fantasy managers should feel good about his outlook once again.

In addition to being projected as a high-scoring affair in the desert, Williams also gets to face a generous Cardinals defense. Arizona is the fourth-friendliest fantasy opponent for wideouts and has given up a league-leading 11 receiving TDs.

DK Metcalf vs. Colts – With Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined with a foot injury, Metcalf will be asked to carry the passing game. His nine targets in Week 4 are a promising sign of things to come and resulted in a 5-115-0 stat line versus the Browns. Indy is not a matchup to be feared.

Romeo Doubs vs. Raiders – With A.J. Brown and now Mack Hollins injured, Doubs has become the focal point of New England's passing attack. Over the last three weeks, he's delivered solid numbers with 96 yards, 49 yards and then his six-catch, 58-yard, two-touchdown explosion in Week 4. The nine targets in that game are what I find the most alluring. Expect Doubs to be featured against a Raiders defense that's permitted 100-yard games to wideouts in back-to-back weeks.

Dohnte Meyers at Dolphins – Tee Higgins seems unlikely to play in Week 5 and Ja'Marr Chase is in a race to be cleared from concussion protocol before Sunday. That puts Meyers in position to start, after his seven-catch, 82-yard performance last week. If Chase sits out as well, Meyers will be a high-end fantasy WR3 with upside. If Chase plays, Meyers can still be started as a WR3/flex.

We can stick with the Bengals when searching for a tight end to start this week. With Chase still working to get cleared and Higgins seeming more doubtful by the day, Gesicki is firmly in play for fantasy.

He's been a sneaky starter most weeks in the opening month, with touchdowns in three of his four outings. Now, he's set to benefit from the receiver injuries and see increased volume against his old team, the Dolphins.

Miami is the fifth-best matchup for fantasy tight ends, allowing George Kittle (80 yards, TD), Travis Kelce (59 yards, TD) and T.J. Hockenson (119 yards) to have big days against them over the past three weeks.

Juwan Johnson vs. Vikings – Suggesting players to start against Minnesota's defense doesn't come without risk. However, the Vikings have given up at least 50 yards to a tight end three times in four weeks and Johnson has posted at least 50 yards in every game. He also has three touchdowns on the season.

Tyler Higbee vs. Bills – With Terrance Ferguson sidelined, Higbee has found the fountain of youth, with 8-62-1 and 5-67-0 stat lines in the last two games. He's worthy of consideration as a streaming option in a potentially high-scoring MNF matchup with the Bills, who are still figuring things out under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard.

They say things can always get worse, but the Eagles are putting that to the test at the moment.

DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley are sidelined, while Dallas Goedert is trying to return from injury after a two-game absence. Wideout Dontayvion Wicks also popped up on the injury report with a new hamstring injury and a limited practice on Thursday.

To make matters worse, the offensive line is in complete disarray following the sudden retirement of Lane Johnson, the trade of Cam Jurgens and a cavalcade of injuries, including Landon Dickerson, Fred Johnson and Drew Kendall.

Now, they're traveling to London to face a Jaguars defense that's known for shutting down the run, but has also been tough on QBs this year. This is not the time to have Hurts in your lineup.

Sam Darnold vs. 49ers – San Francisco is allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks in 2026. The Niners also held Darnold in check during their three meetings last season in Week 1 (150 yards, no TDs), Week 18 (198 yards, no TDs) and the divisional round (124 yards, TD).

Justin Herbert vs. Broncos – Herbert has played so poorly this year (QB22, QB24, QB23, QB27) that he's not even worth starting against a Broncos defense that will be without starting corners Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss.

While it might not have looked pretty at times, Kamara came through for fantasy managers in Week 4 with seven carries for 23 yards, five catches for 35 yards and two touchdowns on Monday Night Football.

Hopefully no one is talking themselves into Kamara being a strong fantasy option after that game. Even with Travis Etienne Jr. on IR, Kamara still only played 38% of the snaps — sharing the load with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson.

Brian Flores' defense isn't going to make life easy on him, either. Prior to Ollie Gordon II's somewhat flukey 100-yard, one-touchdown stat line on just nine carries, the Vikings had held every back they'd faced under 50 rushing yards. On paper, Minnesota is the toughest opponent for fantasy backs in 2026. The 31-year-old Kamara remains a desperation TD-or-bust RB3, who may have trouble holding up to these workloads.

Omarion Hampton vs. Broncos – Hampton's usage is trending in the wrong direction after he split snaps almost evenly with Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal last week. He's managed to salvage his fantasy weeks by scoring touchdowns in three of four games so far, but that won't always be the case. Follow the volume, which led to a season-low 11 touches in Week 4.

Tony Pollard vs. Texans – Pollard has come through with a couple usable stat lines lately, but he's still a risky RB3 with limited scoring upside. Though the Texans defense might not be as ferocious as it was in 2025, I would still be avoiding Pollard in this matchup.

J.K. Dobbins at Chargers – Dobbins has been held under 50 rushing in every game this season, has a very limited role in the passing game and hasn't found the end zone. Even a revenge game narrative against the Chargers isn't enough to convince me to start him.

Vele has been an outstanding fantasy pickup in the opening month, with at least 50 yards in three of his games and a pair of touchdowns.

Coming off a primetime contest where many people watched him catch six passes for 54 yards and a score, fantasy managers might be getting comfortable starting him. I'd advise against it this week.

The Vikings are a challenging defense and Vele has benefitted from some easier matchups in the first four weeks. His only tougher opponent was the Raiders (eighth-fewest fantasy points to WRs), who held him to just three catches for 39 yards. You don't have to drop Vele until Jordyn Tyson returns, just lower your expectations against more difficult opponents like Minnesota.

Eagles WRs vs. Jaguars (London) – This probably goes without saying, but you shouldn't be mining for value on the Eagles' WR depth chart right now. We'll monitor Dontayvion Wicks's status after he showed up with a new injury on Thursday and Makai Lemon remains a deeper stash for later in the season. You just can't trust any of Philly's wideouts in your lineup right now with all the injuries and struggles this offense is dealing with.

Courtland Sutton at Chargers – Sutton has only topped 25 yards in one game this season and is fresh off a one-catch, four-yard effort against the 49ers. Even with Pat Bryant potentially missing time due to injury, Sutton isn't someone I'm willing to put in lineups. Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims Jr. will simply see more work in Bryant's absence.

Wan'Dale Robinson vs. Texans – Robinson has found the end zone in consecutive weeks, but don't get used to it. This is a receiver who hasn't scored more than four touchdowns in an NFL season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling WR4/flex.

After missing last week with an ankle injury, Justin Jefferson has practiced in a limited fashion so far this week. That makes it seem like he's trending in the right direction to play, but remember the Vikings have a Week 6 bye. So, if Minnesota wants to play it safe with the star wideout, he could sit again.

If Jefferson plays, Hockenson goes back to being a low-end TE2 who doesn't qualify as a fantasy starter. However, even if Jefferson is ruled out, fantasy managers should be cautious about chasing Hockenson's 13-catch, 119-yard stat line from last week.

Remember when Dalton Schultz had a 12-catch, 140-yard game for the Texans when Nico Collins was sidelined? Collins remained out the next week, but Schultz drew more defensive attention and flopped with just three catches and 30 yards. Hockenson is in a similar group at the position, making him just a risky streamer.

Dalton Schultz at Titans – Aside from that one big blowup game, Schultz has been kept to 35 yards or less in his three other appearances. That includes just two grabs for nine yards last week.

Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. Ravens – Don't be tempted by Pitts' 47-yard outing last week. It came on just three catches, while running a route on just 43% of the Falcons' dropbacks. He's well off the fantasy radar and should be dropped in most redraft leagues.

articles.title: El salto de 1,42 metros con patines que vale un récord del mundo
articles.standfirst: La rusa Veronika Zherelnikova bate su propia plusmarca mundial de salto de altura con patines
articles.summary: La rusa Veronika Zherelnikova bate su propia plusmarca mundial de salto de altura con patines
articles.body: La rusa Veronika Zherelnikova batió este su propio récord mundial de salto de altura con patines, vigente desde el año pasado, al alcanzar 142 centímetros en la quinta edición de los Juegos Mundiales de Patinaje que se disputan en Asunción (Paraguay). Zherelnikova, de 16 años, había establecido una marca de 140 centímetros para la modalidad durante el torneo de patinaje 'Lishui Open', en agosto pasado en China. Hasta entonces, el récord mundial, con 137 centímetros, la compartían la italiana Francesca Brivio y la francesa Mayrin Burasovitch. El podio lo completaron, con sendos saltos de 127 centímetros, la francesa Emilie Bellanger (plata) y la ucraniana Polina Zelenokhat (bronce)

articles.title: What is the real reason behind World Heavyweight Champion Seth Rollins' delayed WWE television return?
articles.summary: As Seth Rollins has been away from WWE television since SummerSlam, fans have been waiting to see him back in the ring at live events, and they are still
articles.body: As Seth Rollins has been away from WWE television since SummerSlam, fans have been waiting to see him back in the ring at live events, and they are still waiting for him to make a return to WWE RAW. Recent reports suggest that there is a specific reason behind Seth Rollins' absence. A new report has now offered a clearer picture of what’s going on behind the scenes. After losing the World Heavyweight Championship to Roman Reigns at SummerSlam, Rollins stepped away from TV, and now the real reason behind his absence is revealed. Let's take a look at Seth Rollins’ delayed WWE return.WWE reporter Dave Meltzer reveals the reason behind Seth Rollins’ delayed WWE TV returnThe real reason behind Seth Rollins' long hiatus is actually linked to a minor injury. However, reports suggest that the former heavyweight champion could be back on screen very soon. According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter, Rollins is recovering from a minor injury, and WWE has given him additional time to heal. However, the injury is not expected to keep him away much longer, but the company is reportedly waiting for the right opportunity to bring him back.Writing in the latest Wrestling Observer Newsletter, Meltzer stated, “Rollins has what was called a minor injury so they are giving him time to heal up, but he could be back if needed now or soon and the idea is to bring him back for maximum impact when it is right at this point.” (source: Ringside News)Rollins was last seen after losing the World Heavyweight Championship to Roman Reigns at SummerSlam. Since then, he has stepped away from WWE TV till the writing of this report. However, he later revealed that he was healthy enough to wrestle non-televised events during WWE’s South American and Mexico tour. But, he chose to simply take his time and would return when the moment felt right. Speculation also floated that WWE had considered bringing him back at Money in the Bank before changing direction.Meanwhile, WWE superstar Seth Rollins has reportedly landed a new ESPN contract while continuing his successful wrestling career. Apart from appearing in thrilling excitement matches, he will make appearances on several ESPN shows related to sporting events.According to the Sports Business Journal, WWE star Seth Rollins has a separate contract with ESPN for appearances on the network for a limited number of appearances that includes Good Morning Football, First Take, Get Up, and SportsCenter. It will indeed be interesting to witness Rollins in an entirely new role apart from his wrestling skills.Despite expanding his presence in sports media, Rollins has no plans to step away from WWE, though he has only three years remaining on his current WWE contract and has expressed his desire to continue wrestling for as long as he feels he can contribute to the company.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: España mete a seis skaters en la pelea por el Mundial
articles.standfirst: Egoitz Bijueska, Naia Laso y Danny León encabezan una delegación que ha superado el primer corte del Campeonato del Mundo de Park en Asunción
articles.summary: Egoitz Bijueska, Naia Laso y Danny León encabezan una delegación que ha superado el primer corte del Campeonato del Mundo de Park en Asunción
articles.body: Seis españoles siguen adelante en el Mundial de Skateboarding Park de Asunción. La delegación nacional ha superado el primer gran corte de la competición con tres representantes en cada categoría, manteniendo sus opciones de luchar por las medallas en uno de los campeonatos más importantes del calendario internacional. En categoría masculina avanzaron Danny León, Egoitz Bijueska y Alain Kortabitarte, mientras que Naia Laso, Julia Benedetti y Grusha Reyna lograron la clasificación femenina. El resultado confirma la profundidad de un equipo español que combina experiencia internacional, talento emergente y aspiraciones olímpicas. El campeonato llega después de una primera experiencia exigente para dos de los principales referentes españoles. Egoitz Bijueska terminó cuarto en el Mundial de Vert, a las puertas del podio, mientras que Naia Laso fue sexta en la misma disciplina. Ambos afrontan ahora el Park, modalidad incluida en el programa olímpico y en la que han construido buena parte de su trayectoria internacional. También destaca la presencia de Danny León, uno de los skaters españoles con mayor recorrido competitivo, y de Julia Benedetti, sexta en el anterior Mundial de Park. Sus diferentes estilos serán importantes en una competición donde cada ronda exige encontrar el equilibrio entre dificultad, ejecución y aprovechamiento del recorrido. El siguiente objetivo será transformar esa presencia numerosa en puestos de semifinales y finales. España cuenta con seis oportunidades de seguir avanzando, pero el nivel internacional obliga a ejecutar rondas prácticamente perfectas para mantenerse entre los mejores. La competición de Asunción también permite medir el estado del skate español frente a las grandes potencias mundiales, en un ciclo deportivo que tiene como horizonte los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028.

articles.title: Jacob Fatu's WWE status after Jaida Parker’s car attack emerges again in a recent backstage update
articles.summary: As Jacob Fatu was shockingly hit-and-run by Jaida Parker on the September 28 edition of WWE RAW, fresh reports emerged on Fatu's WWE status.
articles.body: As Jacob Fatu was shockingly hit-and-run by Jaida Parker on the September 28 edition of WWE RAW, fresh reports emerged on Fatu's WWE status. Fatu was not seen on the October 5, 2026 edition of WWE RAW, and a new backstage report has revealed why the Bloodline member was kept off the show. In the closing segment of RAW, during the September 28 edition, Jaida Parker crashed her car into Jacob Fatu before joining 946 against The Bloodline.Reports suggest that the storyline was exclusively designed to temporarily remove the WWE star and assign him a new work related to the company. But there seems to be a major update regarding Jacob Fatu's absence from WWE. Let's find out the real reason behind his absence and when Fatu can be expected back inside the ring.WWE backstage update reveals the real reason behind Jacob Fatu's WWE absence after RAW car attackJacob Fatu's recent absence from WWE television reportedly stems from his involvement in filming a project alongside Drew McIntyre and Joe Hendry. According to Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio, the three WWE stars are believed to be in an unspecified show, which could explain why Fatu was written off from television following the car attack angle on RAW.Meltzer also explained that the filming commitment was likely the reason behind Fatu's temporary absence from WWE television. However, the exact nature of the project has not been officially confirmed yet."So the Jacob thing, I believe Jacob and Joe Hendry and Drew McIntyre are doing some WWE show ... so that explains that angle with Jacob,” he added. Meltzer further stated, “The reason he [Fatu]’s out is storyline related, in the sense it wasn’t a cover for being out, but the storyline was to run him over as a part of the storyline regardless.”Actually, as per reports, WWE announced a partnership with ReelShort, a company that produces microdramas, and Fatu, McIntyre, and Hendry are all starring in a new live-action video series for the platform. The project is part of the company's growing efforts to expand its content beyond traditional wrestling programming.His absence comes at a crucial juncture during the Bloodline's ongoing feud with The 946, where Fatu was seen involved in a confrontation with Royce Keys when a black sedan suddenly struck him, and Jaida Parker was seen emerging from the vehicle, where she revealed that she was behind the attack and declared, “Ain't nobody safe,” before leaving alongside Keys and the faction of 946.This angle actually raised questions about Fatu's status and whether WWE was planning to sideline him from the TV for an extended period. However, according to reports related to his return to WWE has not been confirmed yet by the company.Meanwhile, speculation is also hinting at the growing tensions between the two factions, which could lead to a WarGames match at Survivor Series later this year.It is important to note that WWE Survivor Series: WarGames 2026 is scheduled for November 28, although a match between The Bloodline and 946 has not been officially announced.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Watch 13 featured college football games on Oct. 10, including No. 7 Indiana at Nebraska on BIG NOON KICKOFF and No. 2 Georgia at No. 6 Alabama, with TV channels, streaming details and previews.
articles.body: College football Week 6 opens with two unbeaten Big Ten teams at noon ET and builds to a primetime matchup of 5-0 Georgia and Alabama. BIG NOON KICKOFF is in Lincoln, where No. 7 Indiana visits Nebraska on FOX, and No. 5 Ohio State hosts Maryland later in the afternoon. This guide covers eight Saturday games on FOX, FS1 and BTN plus three more national matchups, including No. 1 Texas against Oklahoma in Dallas. This is a curated top-games schedule, not the complete national slate. Rankings reflect the AP Top 25 released Oct. 4. College Football Week 6 Top Games Schedule No. 7 Indiana at Nebraska Indiana and Nebraska are both 5-0 overall and 2-0 in Big Ten play. The Hoosiers beat Rutgers 47-15 last week, and the Cornhuskers beat Maryland 48-23. Indiana's closest game so far was the 29-23 win over Northwestern in Week 4, while Nebraska has won all five of its games by at least 18 points. Indiana won the most recent meeting between the programs, 56-7 in 2024. Ball State at Northwestern Northwestern is 3-1 and 1-1 in the Big Ten, with its lone loss coming 29-23 at Indiana on Sept. 25. Ball State of the MAC enters at 1-4 and has lost three straight, most recently 39-24 to Toledo. The Wildcats beat Penn State 34-13 last week. Ball State's losses include a 56-3 defeat at Ohio State on Sept. 5. No. 22 Houston at Kansas State Houston is 4-1 and 1-1 in the Big 12 after a 27-17 win over UCF, its second straight victory. The Cougars' only loss was 28-26 at Texas Tech. Kansas State is 3-1 and 0-1 in conference play. The Wildcats come off a bye after a 31-26 loss at Cincinnati on Sept. 26. Before that, Kansas State beat Washington State 34-7 and Tulane 31-20. Illinois has lost two straight, to Ohio State and Purdue, most recently 24-17 last week. Michigan State has dropped three in a row, most recently 31-3 at Wisconsin. Michigan State has dropped three in a row, including a 31-3 loss at Wisconsin last week. Maryland at No. 5 Ohio State Ohio State is 4-1 and 2-0 in the Big Ten, with three straight wins since a 24-23 loss at Texas. The Buckeyes won 31-14 at then-No. 14 Iowa last week. Maryland is 2-3 and 0-2 in conference play after three consecutive losses, most recently 48-23 at Nebraska. Nevada at UTEP Nevada (1-3) and UTEP (1-4) are both 0-1 in the Mountain West and have each lost three straight games. UTEP lost 61-7 at New Mexico last week, while Nevada is coming off a bye after a 36-33 loss to Air Force. Nevada comes off a bye after a 36-33 loss to Air Force on Sept. 26. Minnesota at Purdue Minnesota is 4-1 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 20-14 win over Michigan, its third straight victory. The Golden Gophers also won 27-24 at Washington in Week 4, and they beat Purdue 27-20 last season. Purdue is 2-3 and 1-1 in league play after a 24-17 win at Illinois ended a three-game losing streak. It was the Boilermakers' first win since Week 1. Hawaii at Arizona State Arizona State is 2-2 and 1-1 in the Big 12. Hawaii of the Mountain West enters at 1-4. The Sun Devils lost 55-19 to Baylor last week, and the Rainbow Warriors have lost two straight, most recently 20-16 to San Jose State. The nonconference game closes the FOX-family Saturday lineup. FOX, FS1 and BTN games in this guide stream on FOX One. Fans can watch college football on FOX One, subject to the service and plan available in their market. Other Big College Football Games No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma Texas is 4-0 and No. 1 in the AP poll for a fourth straight week. The Longhorns' wins include a 24-23 decision over Ohio State and a 20-17 victory at Tennessee. Oklahoma is 2-2, with losses at Michigan and Georgia. Texas won the last two Red River Rivalry games, 34-3 in 2024 and 23-6 in 2025. Both teams are coming off a Week 5 bye. No. 21 UCLA at No. 13 Oregon UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten, with wins over Purdue and Maryland in league play. Oregon is 3-1, with its only loss coming 39-31 at Oklahoma State. Both teams are coming off a Week 5 bye. The Bruins beat Maryland 54-3 in Week 4, and the Ducks beat USC 41-27. Oregon has won the last five meetings in the series. The teams last played as ranked opponents in 2022. No. 2 Georgia at No. 6 Alabama Georgia and Alabama are both 5-0 overall and 3-0 in the SEC. Georgia beat Vanderbilt 38-14 last week, and Alabama won 56-23 at Mississippi State. The Crimson Tide have scored at least 45 points in each of their five games. The teams split two meetings in 2025, with Alabama winning 24-21 in September and Georgia winning 28-7 in December. How to Watch College Football Week 6 The eight FOX-family games in this guide air on FOX, FS1 or BTN and stream on FOX One. Indiana at Nebraska and Houston at Kansas State air on FOX. Illinois at Michigan State, Nevada at UTEP and Hawaii at Arizona State air on FS1. Ball State at Northwestern, Maryland at Ohio State and Minnesota at Purdue air on BTN. Texas vs. Oklahoma and Georgia at Alabama are available through ESPN Unlimited via the FOX One / ESPN Bundle. UCLA at Oregon airs on CBS. Subscriptions, authentication requirements and availability vary by service, plan and location. Check local listings before kickoff. College football times and network assignments can change during the week. The Week 6 FOX-family Saturday starts with Indiana at Nebraska at noon ET and ends with Hawaii at Arizona State at 10:30 p.m. ET, and the national schedule also features ranked matchups UCLA at Oregon and Georgia at Alabama.

articles.title: Potente terremoto en Panamá de magnitud superior a 8 sacude varias ciudades de Colombia: hay alerta
articles.standfirst: Terremoto hoy en Panamá y Colombia: SGC entrega reporte oficial sobre sismo de magnitud superior a 8
articles.summary: Terremoto hoy en Panamá y Colombia: SGC entrega reporte oficial sobre sismo de magnitud superior a 8
articles.body: Un fuerte sismo de magnitud 8.0 se registró este viernes 9 de octubre de 2026 a las 12:56 p. m. (hora local), con epicentro localizado en territorio panameño. El fenómeno telúrico, por su gran magnitud y profundidad superficial, se sintió con considerable intensidad en diversas regiones del centro, occidente y costa Caribe de Colombia. Según la información consolidada por el Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC) en coordinación con agencias internacionales como el USGS (United States Geological Survey): Al tratarse de una profundidad menor a 30-35 kilómetros, la energía liberada se transmitió de forma directa a la superficie, lo que provocó una fuerte sacudida en las zonas pobladas cercanas e impulsó la propagación de ondas hacia el territorio colombiano. A los pocos minutos del evento, ciudadanos en ciudades como Medellín, Cartagena, Montería, Cali, San Andrés y varias zonas del departamento del Chocó reportaron el movimiento telúrico. En múltiples edificaciones de gran altura e instituciones públicas se activaron los protocolos de emergencia y evacuación preventiva. Las autoridades de Gestión del Riesgo en Colombia iniciaron de inmediato un barrido nacional para evaluar posibles afectaciones estructurales o personas lesionadas, con especial atención en los departamentos limítrofes con Panamá y la costa del Océano Pacífico. Debido a la magnitud del terremoto y su localización cercana a las zonas costeras del Pacífico panameño, los organismos de monitoreo oceánico y marítimo mantuvieron bajo observación constante el comportamiento de las mareas ante cualquier variación anómala en la costa del Pacífico y el mar Caribe. Las entidades de socorro instan a la comunidad a mantener la calma, informarse únicamente a través de los boletines oficiales del Servicio Geológico Colombiano y las coordinaciones de Gestión del Riesgo, y verificar el estado de sus viviendas e instalaciones antes de reingresar.

articles.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson Ruled Out For Week 5, Tyler Huntley Set To Start
articles.summary: Ravens' quarterback Lamar Jackson has officially been ruled out for Week 5 against the Falcons. Tyler Huntley will start in his place.
articles.body: The Baltimore Ravens will be without their star quarterback this week, as Lamar Jackson has officially been ruled out for the Week 5 matchup against the Falcons. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will make his first start of the season in Jackson's place. "We have a ton of confidence in [Huntley] to play really well," head coach Jesse Minter said of Huntley’s start on Sunday. "I think everyone on the team is excited to see that." Jackson has been battling an ankle injury following the Week 4 loss to the Tennessee Titans. Although he didn't suffer a long-term injury, his status against the Falcons was up for debate and not guaranteed. The Ravens offense has already been dealing with a few injuries, specifically with wide receivers Ja’Kobi Lane and Zay Flowers in Week 1; Flowers returned from his hamstring injury, while Lane remains on injured reserve with a fractured wrist. In his 12 starts across his six seasons in a Ravens jersey, Huntley has compiled a 5-6 record. Huntley last started for Baltimore on Jan. 4, when he led the Ravens to a 41-24 win over the Green Bay Packers. Minter enters the Sunday night matchup with a 3-1 record as head coach. In his first game without Jackson, Minter will need to lead the offense past the Falcons' defense to secure a 4-1 start to the season. Coincidentally, the last time the Ravens faced the Falcons in a regular-season game was in 2022, when Huntley started for Baltimore and led the team to a 17-9 win. Sin embargo, Coelho detuvo el lanzamiento y prolongó la resistencia portuguesa, después de que España hubiera convertido todas sus penas máximas anteriores en el campeonato. La insistencia lusa encontró premio a dos minutos del final, cuando Catarina Costa transformó un penalti para establecer el 2-1 y reabrir un encuentro que parecía encarrilado para las españolas. articles.title: Africa Cup of Nations may stay as a biennial event, says CAF chief Motsepe
articles.summary: CAF had declared the Africa Cup of Nations would be held every four years, but may reverse that decision.
articles.body:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) is reappraising its decision to hold the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, CAF president Patrice Motsepe declared on Friday, while insisting his organisation did not take orders from FIFA or UEFA.

Motsepe, who last December announced the biennial AFCON would switch to a four-year cycle from 2028, said on Friday that it was “nonsense, absolute rubbish” that CAF was being dictated to by either the world or European governing body.

The decision at the time, bringing the competition to a schedule that aligned with FIFA’s international calendar, rankled many at the 2025 AFCON in Morocco, with some saying it was made with European wishes at heart to the detriment of African interests.

Motsepe, a South African billionaire who is also a vice-president of FIFA, appeared stung by the criticism.

“My No. 1 job, my No. 1 duty is to protect, promote, and advance the interests of Africa,” he said. “And there are times when I have to stand firm and say, ‘Listen, we’re going to fight on this issue.’ And there are times when I have to say, ‘No.’

“The AFCON — because this is one of the issues we’re talking about — we took a decision as Africa because there were lots of issues, but I can guarantee you we have discussed it over the last few days to say we are looking at everything, including having the AFCON coming back every two years,” Motsepe said. “We’re very clear.”

He was speaking at the final day of CAF’s three-day strategy conference in Cape Verde. On Thursday, he reiterated the 54-member body’s “unanimous” support for FIFA’s under-fire president Gianni Infantino, and Infantino reminded his potential election voters of investments FIFA has made for African football since gaining the job 10 years ago.

Motsepe reaffirmed the 2027 Africa Cup will go ahead as planned in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda next year, despite recent media reports from France saying construction projects were not going to schedule and some CAF members were pushing to have the tournament moved.

“You have to believe in Africa. There will be problems, there will be failures, fine, but we will be there. That’s what Mandela taught us,” Motsepe said.

articles.title: Panthers say Brad Marchand needs 6 weeks before he can resume play
articles.summary: Yes, the Florida Panthers are already seeing injuries piling up.
articles.body:
SUNRISE, Fla. — Yes, the Florida Panthers are already seeing injuries piling up.

And yes, the Panthers know things could be much, much worse.

Florida forward Brad Marchand will need six weeks to recover from his left leg injury and should be able to resume play with the Panthers sometime in November, coach Paul Maurice confirmed Friday. That comes on the heels of forward Aleksander Barkov being expected to need a similar timetable before he can play again, also because of a left leg injury.

Losing two stars isn't good. But Maurice sees the silver lining.

"Nobody said 'months' yet," Maurice said.

That's the difference between the injuries this season and what was happening to Florida at this point last season. By then, Barkov was already expected to be sidelined at least seven months with torn ligaments in his right knee and Matthew Tkachuk was also going to be out for multiple months while recovering from surgery to repair a sports hernia and torn adductor.

Barkov wound up missing the entire season. Tkachuk didn't start his season until mid-January. The Panthers saw players miss a combined 544 games with injuries last season and missed the playoffs, an unceremonious end to their run as back-to-back Stanley Cup champions.

So, yes, losing Barkov (who could be back by the end of November) and Marchand (who'll be back on the ice in three weeks, then is expected to need three more weeks to rehab and condition) for a few weeks now isn't ideal. But Florida has been there before.

"We're no stranger to guys going down the last few years and guys have done a great job of stepping up," Tkachuk said. "Worst case, you just got to win 1-0, 2-1."

There have been clear sighs of relief with the knowledge that Barkov and Marchand will both return in a few weeks. Florida was short-handed in all four games of its season-opening road trip — Marchand missed the first two, Barkov missed the next two, and defenseman Aaron Ekblad also missed two because he and his wife were welcoming a baby — and the Panthers went 2-0-2 anyway.

Ekblad is expected to be in the lineup when Florida plays its home opener Saturday against Minnesota.

"There's a threshold to this," Maurice said. "You can only survive so many (injuries) and we proved that. But you get two or three guys out, it's standard operating procedure in the National Hockey League. That's just normal. You prefer it's not your No. 1 at any one position because those guys hurt to lose. Everybody's got two or three. And then, you know, you get to five, it starts to get a little tight. Anything over five, you start to really feel it."

articles.title: Cowboys' 'mind boggling' defense is back to square one, whether coaches admit it or not
articles.summary: After five games, the unit has made little improvement from last year against the run and the pass.
articles.body:
FRISCO – The Cowboys defense is back to square one.

The man who signs the checks, Jerry Jones, said it after his team's 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay late Thursday night.

Jones reiterated his comments Friday morning during a radio interview on 105.3 The Fan.

"Surprising isn't even a big enough word," the team owner told KRLD-FM. "It's mind boggling looking at the stats of our last five games."

The coach, Brian Schottenheimer, respectfully disagreed with the idea that defense is back to square one. Injuries are part of the problem with the Cowboys ' defense, but after five games, this team has made little gains over last year.

After five games, the Cowboys have given up 27.2 points per game. That's three fewer points than last year over the same time span. When it comes to total yards, the defense has allowed 1,977 yards, just 83 fewer yards than last season.

In the first five weeks, the Cowboys defense allowed nearly 500 more passing yards than last year's group.

On the season, the Cowboys front has allowed teams to gain 842 rushing yards. That's last in the NFL.

The next closet team is the Carolina Panthers, and they've given up 261 fewer rushing yards. By the way, the Panthers are off this week, so the Cowboys' defense can maintain the "worst run defense in the league" title for another few weeks.

And speaking of that run defense, Jones invested draft capital and a contract extension for a little over $100 million for defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . Jones also approved trading an elite pass rusher Micah Parsons for Kenny Clark.

He's getting next to nothing out of them, especially on Thursday night.

"The thing that probably bothers me the most [Thursday night] is how they ran between the tackles," Jones said after the game about the Buccaneers' 241 rushing yards. "So [they're] able to have that running game in there with them where we have a lot of strength and so that's something that we've got to really look at and will."

The Cowboys stressed the pass rush would improve this season with the maturity of second-year player Donovan Ezeiruaku, trading for Rashan Gary, spending a first-round pick on Malachi Lawrence and signing Von Miller . It hasn't.

On Thursday night, the Cowboys had just one quarterback hit on undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels.

He looked poised and confident against the Cowboys' defense .

Lawrence had the one quarterback hit, on a sack. It was the first of his career.

Miller, who said he could roll out of bed and get eight sacks, has none through five weeks.

Schottenheimer said Miller didn't play much because he's more of a situational player.

But with a defense struggling, you need the aging veteran to start turning back the clock, if he can.

If not, then maybe James Houston, who had 5 ½ sacks last season, should become active on gamedays.

The linebackers are up and down, starting with rookie Jaishawn Barham as the middle linebacker. Whenever DeMarvion Overshown returns from his hamstring injury, moving him to weakside might help.

Cornerback DaRon Bland dropped an interception for a potential pick-six against Tampa Bay that would have given his team a chance to tie the score late in the fourth quarter. Bland also gave up a long pass completion as he fell on a double move.

Joey Porter Jr. was supposed to start at the other corner spot Thursday night but an illness sent him home . Ineffective play was left with Porter gone.

You have questions about why safety Caleb Downs is playing so far away from the line of scrimmage. He's playing deep safety, but you wonder if he's better suited to play near the line of scrimmage to help the run defense and maybe, hey, blitz.

Downs, the first-round pick, recorded his first sack of his career when blitzing.

The scheme doesn't make sense. The coaching doesn't make sense. The playing doesn't make sense.

It's all a disaster five weeks into the season. Things were supposed to get better. and instead it's spinning out of control.

Defensive coordinator Christian Parker isn't going anywhere . But he and the staff need to find solutions before the man who signs the checks starts looking at resumes again.

As every Heisman Trophy contender knows, college football has a lot of talent. But only one player wins the trophy. Winning the Heisman is a one-way ticket to the top of the NFL draft. Fernando Mendoza, Travis Hunter, Jayden Daniels and Caleb Williams are four of countless previous winners who have punched their ticket in this way.

Keeping that in mind, here's a look at the top 10 players who have made a solid case to win the award heading into the Week 6 slate, including Malachi Toney, Jeremiah Smith, and more.

Top 10 Heisman Contenders To Know Heading into Week 6

#10 – Princewill Umanmielen, DE, LSU Tigers

Princewill Umanmielen has gotten to the quarterback better than anyone else in college football with eight sacks so far this season. Defense isn't typically thought of in connection with the Heisman, but if anyone has a shot this season, it is Umanmielen. He will need to keep pace to overcome the others ahead of him, however.

#9 – Dylan Riley, RB, Boise State Broncos

Dylan Riley leads college football in total rushing yards, which automatically puts him into consideration. Riley is also over 6.3 yards per carry, which makes him reliable, and has scored five touchdowns on the ground. However, he still has room for improvement to have a shot at winning the award over the other names.

The quarterback is third in passing touchdowns and second in passing yards. Malachi Toney has dominated this season with 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. He doesn't lead college football in either category, which is why he's not at the top of the list. Plus, it is historically harder for a receiver to win the Heisman, which will hold back the other receiver ahead of him as well.

Jeremiah Smith is first in receptions, yards, and receiving touchdowns. If there is a wide receiver that is going to win the Heisman, it is Smith. Since 2020, two receivers have won the award, which makes him a serious contender to win in 2026.

Gunner Stockton is tied for ninth in touchdown passes and is third in passer rating at 202.1 (ESPN). As such, Stockton is a top contender to win the Heisman. It also helps to be part of a program with plenty of visibility on any given week.

The match will be the final road match of the regular season for SAFC, which sits above the playoff line in eighth place in the USL Western Conference table. SAFC goalkeeper Joey Batrouni said the club knows what is at stake going into the match in Oakland.

"I think we've been more focused than we have been all season," Batrouni said. "I think it's come to the realization and reality has kind of hit in that we need a win and we need those points because Las Vegas and Phoenix are creeping up on us (in the playoff race). The morale has been there, and everybody knows that and I think we're just focused on getting points and however we do that, we do that."

Last week, SAFC fell to Las Vegas Lights SC 1-0 in Las Vegas, marking the third consecutive match San Antonio was shut out. The Lights scored their lone goal of the match in the final minutes of the first half, which came as Manuel Arteaga fired a shot into the net off a deflected save by Batrouni, who was up in the box.

SAFC created nine shot attempts in the second half but could not get a goal for the equalizer.

Defender Akeem O'Connor-Ward said he isn't feeling any more pressure on the defensive end despite SAFC's recent offensive struggles on the pitch.

"I think we've been doing well (defensively) the past couple of games," O'Connor-Ward said. "I think it was just a lapse, an error, which led to a goal (Las Vegas). Joey (Batrouni) made a good save, but we weren't there to follow up. But as a defensive side, I think we're pretty sound."

While SAFC has been solid on the defensive side, O'Connor-Ward said they need to find a way to score goals, which San Antonio hasn't done since a 2-1 loss to Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC on Sept. 11.

"We worked on it again this week, going back to fundamentals (defensively)," O'Connor-Ward said. "Nothing crazy I think on our end defensively, just figuring out a way to be more cohesive in the attacking area and more times than not finish chances, whether it be set pieces, run a play. Just figuring out how to put the ball in there."

Injuries have added to SAFC's struggles, as midfielder Jorge Hernandez - one of the club's top scorers - has been out the past two games with an injury and midfielder Nicky Hernandez and forward Andres Paredes had to leave the Las Vegas match with injuries.

SAFC coach Carlos Llamosa said it has been frustrating having to deal with injuries during the final stretch of the season, but that the team will have to move forward with the players they have.

"We're going to miss Nicky, we're going to miss Andres," Llamosa said. "But the other players we have here, they have the quality to step in and do the job. Make sure they recover and hopefully come back for playoffs and concentrate and focus on the guys that we have healthy here."

Oakland, which has won two of its last four matches, is led by forward Peter Wilson, who has 13 goals, making him one of the top four scorers in the league, while forward Wolfgang Prentice has chipped in five goals.

"Wilson is one of the top forwards in this league," Llamosa said. "Our defenders, especially our center backs through the season, they've been good against those types of forwards. They know who they are playing against. It's not the first time they're going to play against them. I know they (Oakland) have a couple of key players but as a team they play really well. So, we have to be engaged and ready to play against anybody on that team."

In their last meeting against the Roots at Toyota Field in August, SAFC lost 1-0, with Oakland scoring the game-winning goal on a penalty kick from Wilson in the 90th minute. The penalty kick was set up when Batrouni was whistled for a yellow card as he pushed Wilson, as both players were going for a loose ball near the goal line.

Batrouni is using the memory from that loss as motivation going into Oakland as SAFC aims for a pivotal win.

"I think I would like to avenge that and hopefully get three points when we go up there, and it also be nice for the team morale with three games left going into the playoffs," Batrouni said. "I think we get this win and it will kind of take a lot of pressure off our shoulders and kind of let us focus a little bit more on the playoffs."

articles.title: Jaguars vs. Eagles: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 5
articles.summary: Big Cat Country previews the Jaguars’ Week 5 matchup against the Eagles.
articles.body:
Welcome to Big Cat Country's staff roundtable!

Today, we're previewing Week 5's matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles.

Question 1: What questions do you still have about the Jaguars, if any, after they beat the Bengals last week?

Dillon Appleman : I know the defense made the big stop at the end eventually, but I really need to see more execution from that side of the ball in crunch time. In Week 2 against the Broncos, and this past week against the Bengals, both opposing offenses had long, seemingly easy drives down the field when it mattered most late in the game. I would like to see more of a blood-in-the-water style of play in those situations going forward.

Travis Holmes : Can this Jacksonville squad handle the weight of expectations? Heading into Jacksonville's Week 2 game, heaps of praise were heaped upon this Jaguars team as a top AFC Super Bowl contender, only for them to fail to play the game we know they're capable of the following week. In a week-by-week, matchup-by-matchup league, losses will happen, but Jacksonville clearly didn't play its style of football against Denver. It was this inconsistency issue that has plagued the team for years. Similarly, Jacksonville is once again the national media's "Belle of the Ball" this week, with talking heads coming out of every corner of the media sphere to praise this team's future prospects. Can they tune out the noise and handle today's business?

Gus Logue : Where are the deep passes? Trevor Lawrence has thrown the ball 10+ yards downfield on 43.3% of his attempts — the highest rate in the league, per NFL Pro — but most of that production has come in the intermediate area. He ranks eighth in pass attempts 10-19 yards downfield (37) and just 25th in pass attempts 20+ yards downfield (8). It's good that Jacksonville's offense has been lighting up scoreboards without relying on shot plays. But the team does have Brian Thomas Jr., after all. It would be nice to see a couple of deep passes completed against a talented secondary.

Henry Zimmer : My big question will be how good the offensive line can be in terms of protecting Trevor Lawrence and keeping the running game going. Overall, the offensive line did OK against a solid Bengals front but the games never get easier as they go. This unit needs to find its footing, find its right five guys. When that happens, this team could be special.

Question 2: What's the key to a Jaguars victory this week?

Dillon : It's a bit simple, but it's just to win the turnover battle. The Eagles are snakebittin with injuries more than just about any team in the league right now, so really it'll come down to not gifting a desperate team favorable opportunities via turnovers or mistakes. Clean execution and not forcing anything should lead to a positive outcome.

Travis : Ezra Cleveland and Robert Hainsey versus Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Moro Ojomo will be the matchup that determines this game's outcome, in my estimation. Vic Fangio's defense has struggled to consistently pressure quarterbacks this season when not blitzing, ranking 16th in the NFL with a 31% pressure rate when rushing 4 or less. That's while playing a defensive scheme specifically built around getting home with four. Jalen Carter has clearly seemed limited as a pass rusher while playing with a cast on his right wrist due to a hairline fracture, in a similar manner to Travon Walker in 2025. However, given Hainsey and Cleveland's slower start to 2026, Carter is likely still dangerous enough with his power rushes to disrupt the pocket for Trevor.

Gus : Winning the explosive-play battle. I don't expect Vic Fangio to allow Lawrence to paper-cut his defense to death by taking short, efficient passes and checking into runs against light boxes all game long. The Jaguars will need to make a few plays on offense. On defense, they really just need to avoid getting Mossed — because without multiple Pro Bowlers surrounding him, Jalen Hurts just isn't that good by himself.

Henry : This could be another "don't play with your food" game for Jacksonville. Just go out and win. Your key is to beat a banged-up team that is in free fall. This roster, at least on paper, is better than Cleveland's but the process is the same. You are supposed to win, so go out and do it for 60 minutes.

Question 3: Who will be an X-factor for the Jaguars on Sunday?

Dillon : Bhayshul Tuten. Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence get most of the attention for the Jaguars, but the impact of Bhayshul Tuten this season has been undeniable. He's third in the league in success rate, as well as missed tackles forced, which has been huge considering the middling performance of the offensive line to this point. I expect Sunday to be a heavy workload for the young back.

Travis : An often-overlooked area may come front and center this week. With an extensive Eagles injury report heading into the London matchup, most attention has gone to the starting players who may or may not be available. However, I believe this creates a huge opportunity for Heath Farwell's special teams unit to be this week's biggest X-factor. When so many starting-level players have been either traded, placed on injured reserve, or simply injured this week, that forces many practice squad, rotational depth, or recently signed players into increased special teams opportunities. A missed block, missed tackle, missed assignment, or miscommunication in a key situation could be all it takes to bust Sunday's game wide open for Jacksonville.

Gus : Travon Walker. In case you didn't hear, future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement after missing last week's game due to personal reasons. Our friends at Bleeding Green Nation believe third-round rookie Markel Bell will draw his second NFL start over veteran swing tackle (and former Jaguar) Fred Johnson. Walker should be licking his chops to face a young buck following his 1-pressure performance against Amarius Mims. On top of that, it's no secret that Jalen Hurts is much more efficient when rolling out to his right than his left. Even if Walker doesn't destroy Bell on every snap, he's got to contain Hurts.

Henry : My X-Factor for Sunday morning is Anthony Campanile. He should be able to feast upon the remnants of this bad Eagles offense. With potentially no DeVonta Smith or Saquon Barkley, this could be a very long afternoon for new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion.

What are your Week 5 predictions, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments!

articles.summary: Four of the six cornerbacks on the Patriots roster have been ruled out for Week 5.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots ruled out six players for their upcoming Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, and four of them are members of their cornerback group.

Starters Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis will miss the contest due to respective shoulder and neck injuries, as will backups Karon Prunty and Channing Canada, who are both dealing with hamstring issues. Needless to say, this leaves the team quite thin at the position heading into a game against one of the most productive passing offenses in the NFL so far this season.

Let's therefore reset the depth chart ahead of Sunday's meeting with Kirk Cousins and the Raiders offense.

53-man roster: Christian Gonzalez (0) , Carlton Davis III (7) , Marcus Jones (25 | PR), Charles Woods (22), Channing Canada (29) , Karon Prunty (21) Practice squad: Kindle Vildor (28), Al'zillion Hamilton (26)

53-man roster: Christian Gonzalez (0) , Carlton Davis III (7) , Marcus Jones (25 | PR), Charles Woods (22), Channing Canada (29) , Karon Prunty (21)

Practice squad: Kindle Vildor (28), Al'zillion Hamilton (26)

As of Friday afternoon, the Patriots have only four healthy cornerbacks available between their roster and practice squad. On the 53-man team, Marcus Jones and Charles Woods are the only options left, and naturally expected to see considerable playing time on Sunday.

That said, even they are not at a 100%. Woods, who got banged up during last week's win over the Buffalo Bills, is also listed on the injury report: he is questionable with a shoulder injury.

Considering this, both of Kindle Vildor and recent addition Al'zillion Hamilton getting elevated from the practice squad on Saturday seems like a foregone conclusion. In addition, the team has also started experimenting with safety Jaylen Reed as more of a nickel option in practice; he too could factor into the mix come Sunday.

As things currently stand, however, the starting trio at cornerback will likely consist of Jones, Woods and Vildor.

The San Francisco 49ers have had to make due without one of their best players the last couple of weeks, as defensive end Nick Bosa has been sidelined with a calf injury that he suffered in practice.

While it was originally believed that Bosa could miss significant time, and even possibly the rest of the season, he believes he could be back on the field in the near future.

According to NBC Sports' Matt Maiocco, Bosa said that he's "pretty darn likely" to play in the team's Monday night game against the Washington Commanders in Week 6.

That would be a huge boost to a 49ers defense that recorded two sacks in Week 3 and didn't take down Bo Nix even once in Week 4.

In his two games this year since returning from a torn ACL that ended his 2025 campaign prematurely, he's recorded seven tackles, two tackles for a loss and one quarterback hit. Even if Bosa isn't getting home, he's still impacting most passing downs, as he can speed up a quarterback's decision-making or draw attention away from his teammates who can then recorded sacks or quarterback hits themselves.

Either way, it will be great to have Bosa back on the field whenever he gets out there.

articles.title: Mercedes Left with Head Scratching after Russell & Antonelli’s Split Strategy in Singapore
articles.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli had no grip, as George Russell could see the old package also working well in the F1 Singapore GP, as Mercedes faced head scratching. A...
articles.body:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli had no grip, as George Russell could see the old package also working well in the F1 Singapore GP, as Mercedes faced head scratching.

After little answers in Malaysia, Mercedes decided to split the package for this weekend's F1 Singapore GP . The 2026 points leader Antonelli is running the new package, while Russell is on the old as they extend the use even during sprint qualifying .

The results show Russell finishing second, while Antonelli is a lowly seventh. It is exactly the result that Mercedes did not want, not because of any bias, but it has left them with more questions than any answer that they were looking for.

Russell agrees that the old package seems to be working, but he feels it does not prove that the updated package is not 100% working. He knows that the results speak for itself and accepts that it hasn't worked till now, but it is also not showing that it isn't working.

Russell Mixed on Package, Nothing Says New Not Working

"I think we've seen competitive all day to be honest from the first laps in FP1," Russell said to the media. "We obviously topped the timesheets there. When Lewis, Max was fast , and he went on a slightly different strategy to us in Q3 just doing one lap.

"Who knows what was best, but pretty satisfied with the P2. We can definitely confirm the old one is not bad, let's see what tomorrow brings with Kimi on the upgrade. As a team, there's still nothing telling us that it isn't working, but it's more driven by the stopwatch and, yeah, the stopwatch has not been great for the upgrade yet.

"So, let's see and yeah, maybe somewhere else is a different day," summed up Russell, as teammate Antonelli expanded on his struggles. The Italian notes how different the car is to drive from earlier in the season, which is making his run more difficult.

Antonelli Highlights Unpredictability with New Package

He did not go into the details, but highlighted the unpredictability and tricky aspect. He doesn't have hope of finding the missing time in main F1 qualifying either, but noted that they will churn out the data to see what can be done to improve the situation.

"Yes and no, to be fair, already at FP1 I was struggling and, yeah, still a lot to understand about this package," said Antonelli to the media. "It's really the car is very difficult, very unpredictable and very difficult to put a lap together.

"So yeah, it's a shame because I was coming with high hopes, but so far, it's been very difficult. I think it's going to be a difficult weekend unless we can pull something out tomorrow, but other than that, it's going to be very tricky. I don't really see where we can find seven tenths, but you never know.

"Maybe tonight, with Bono, the engineer, we're going to find something in the car. And for sure, I'm going to try to improve a little bit the driving and then let's see, we'll see tomorrow where we end up," summed up Antonelli, who still holds a good advantage over Russell and his rivals, in terms of the points.

As for Mercedes, Andrew Shovlin admits there was a lot of head scratching inside the F1 team after a difficult Friday in Singapore after splitting the package. The result of Russell has only added to their misery, even though it is a front-row start for the Brit.

"After a difficult weekend in Malaysia, we decided to run our cars in split specification this weekend here in Singapore," said Shovlin. "It is not the easiest track to do that at, or have the Sprint format, as it often takes a bit of time to get the car set-up dialled in.

"We've seen that today as whilst we're pleased to see George on the front row, it has left us with a bit of head scratching to do to understand why the update is not bringing the performance step we expect."

Shovlin Expands on Antonelli's Struggles

Expanding a bit on the issues, Shovlin said Antonelli suffered from a lack of confidence in braking and entry phase. It seems it is down to what the Italian said about the unpredictability of the F1 car, which is hurting his confidence in tackling a corner.

"Neither car had a great balance, although Kimi was lacking more confidence on the braking and entry phase and that's what you need to attack a qualifying lap here," continued Shovlin. "We'll keep working to understand why that's the case. We've got plenty of data around us to try and make some progress and, hopefully we'll be able to get Kimi's car in a better place for main qualifying tomorrow."

articles.title: Steelers DB Unexpectedly Listed as Questionable
articles.summary: Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was unexpectedly listed as questionable when the Pittsburgh Steelers came out with their Week 5 injury report […]
articles.body:
Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was unexpectedly listed as questionable when the Pittsburgh Steelers came out with their Week 5 injury report on Friday afternoon.

Ramsey has been playing through a fractured right wrist that he suffered in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals. He broke his wrist in the first quarter of that game, and didn't miss a single snap of action.

He was limited in practice in all three Week 4 sessions, but once again played a normal workload against the Cleveland Browns last Thursday night.

With the extra time off, it seemed likely that Ramsey would be good to go entering Week 5, but he missed practice on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday and Friday, prompting the team to list him as questionable to face to the Indianapolis Colts this Sunday.

Ramsey said he tries to play through the pain when he can, but admitted that even he has his limits in that regard.

"I just like playing football, so I try to tough it out when I can," he said on Friday. "You can't all the time."

If Ramsey were to miss Sunday's game or not be able play his normal workload, veteran backup Brandin Echols would likely step into his slot cornerback role, with the combination of Jaquan Brisker , Robert Spears-Jennings and Rayshawn Jenkins picking up the safety portion of Ramsey's two-pronged role.

The Steelers will have their final practice of the week on Saturday before Sunday's game and could adjust Ramsey's injury status at that time.

articles.title: Takeaways from the Open Practice
articles.summary: Reactions from a 90 minute practice
articles.body:
NC State held practice at Lenovo today (10/9) and opened it to the public. It was a normal practice, not something special put on for the viewing audience. After the practice they gave Coach Gainey a mic to speak to the crowd. He smiled and yelled

He said that 2,000 people had RSVP'd to attend, but they didn't know the actual number of attendees. There was a surprising number of people there for a Friday afternoon.

The Pack will scrimmage with ECU Saturday. It will be on the practice court at the Dail Center. We are not invited. So don't tell anybody.

Starting with the bad news. Coach Vasiljevic has a torn Achilles tendon and is in a cast. He is not expected to play at all this season. But he was on the sidelines contributing as best as he could during practice. He seemed in good spirits when we spoke.

Otherwise, the players were all in attendance and played.

Practice was non-stop. As Coach Gainey previously mentioned, that is intentional for conditioning. There was one short water break, plus some coaching moments where they sat and listened.

During the defensive drills, you immediately noticed the physicality. The defender was in contact with the ball handler and fighting through screens. Excited to see that during a game.

Shah Hall – The most impressive play of the afternoon was by Shah Hall. During a short scrimmage, he blocked a 3PT shot, then chased it down before it got out of bounds and tipped it to Paul McNeil for an easy layup. As we have heard, he's a heck of an athlete and can really, really jump.

Paul McNeil – At one point he had a lightly contested 3PT shot and chose to drive around the defender and take it to the basket. He looked good doing it. At another point, he stepped out and blocked a 3PT shot.

Christian Hammond – Really nice stroke. Shot 3PT well, took it to the basket well, and hit his free throws.

articles.title: Clemson makes its position clear on PCSA amid ‘Gang of Four’ accusation
articles.summary: Clemson released a statement on the Protect College Sports Act on Friday afternoon, following one North Carolina put out earlier in the day. Both statements...
articles.body:
Clemson released a statement on the Protect College Sports Act on Friday afternoon, following one North Carolina put out earlier in the day. Both statements arrived after a lobbying group that supports the bill accused the two schools, along with Florida State and Miami, of endangering it in the House.

Clemson's statement backs the bill and the bipartisan effort behind it in its opening lines before turning to the realignment fight.

"Clemson has consistently supported the PCSA while advocating for a narrowly tailored provision addressing conference composition. This critical flexibility would strengthen the legislation without undermining its core objectives," Clemson said in the statement. "Clemson is not seeking to delay or derail the PCSA. We are working to ensure the final legislation protects the ability of institutions to adapt, compete and succeed at all levels."

The "delay or derail" line answers Saving College Sports, the group self-funded by Texas Tech booster Cody Campbell. In a statement shared on Thursday, the group branded Clemson, North Carolina, Florida State and Miami a "Gang of Four" that wants "to either get out of the conference or break it apart." It also argued their amendment would sunset the provision so they could leave the ACC immediately.

North Carolina answered first, and the two statements share the same vocabulary. "Supporting the bill and seeking to improve it are not in conflict," UNC said in its statement. "Congress can protect college sports without litigating conference composition, and we look forward to working with the House to get this legislation enacted," the school added.

What would Clemson's 'narrowly tailored' change actually allow?

The presidents and chancellors of the four schools sent a letter last week to House Speaker Mike Johnson asking for two edits. One raises the bill's cap on conference membership from 20 schools to 22. The other removes the requirement that a school leaving one covered conference spend three years as an independent before joining another.

The Big Ten has 18 members and the SEC has 16, so a 20-school ceiling leaves room for two more Big Ten schools and four more in the SEC. At 22, those openings become four and six. Dropping the independence period would also spare a departing school three years without the conference revenue distributions it collects now.

Clemson sued the ACC over its exit fees in 2024, a year after Florida State did. The eventual settlement made 2030-31 the season the fee levels off around $75 million per school.

ACC commissioner Jim Phillips has described a 14-to-4 split inside his league. "It's rare to have unanimity on anything as it relates to a bill," Phillips said on Tuesday at ACC basketball media days in Charlotte. "We have 14 schools that feel really good about it that want to sign it, and we have four schools that have an issue with a portion of it, so that's what I'm going to continue to push toward the decisionmakers and those that have written the bill to date."

The Senate passed the bill 77-22 on Sept. 28. House Republican leadership has said it will not call members back to vote before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

articles.title: Can No. 12 Utes keep it rolling against Kansas and get Scalley off to best start by a Utah coach?
articles.summary: After a 5-0 start to his head coaching career, which began with a Las Vegas Bowl victory last season, Scalley needs just one more win to set the record for b...
articles.body:
A lot has gone right for Morgan Scalley's Utes in 2026.

Despite replacing the entire starting offensive line, most of the starters on the defensive line and a good chunk of the coaching staff, including heralded offensive line coach Jim Harding and offensive coordinator Jason Beck, the Utes have hit the ground running in Scalley's inaugural season as the head coach.

By just about any metric, the Utes are one of the best teams in college football.

Utah ranks No. 11 in the nation in total offense, No. 12 in scoring offense, No. 15 in total defense and No. 3 in scoring defense. In all but one quarter of Utah's schedule, the Utes have been dominant, often putting games to bed by the beginning of the fourth quarter.

Sure, Utah's schedule hasn't exactly been a murderers' row, but all the Utes can do is play who is in front of them, and they've responded by beating every opponent by at least 14 points.

Quarterback Devon Dampier has been efficient , throwing for 896 yards and nine touchdowns with just one interception on a 70.3% completion percentage, while adding 135 yards and two scores on the ground.

Wayshawn Parker has staked his claim as one of the Big 12's premier running backs with 328 yards and five touchdowns on the ground and 154 yards and four scores as a receiver, and receiver Braden Pegan has emerged as a go-to threat for the offense.

Offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven has made Ute fans forget about Beck with his creative and effective offense that features two quarterbacks (Dampier and Byrd Ficklin) and a variety of interesting formations and plays.

"I think the whole idea was being multiple and trying to distribute the football and getting everybody involved, making defenses have to defend the whole field and not knowing where the ball's going to land," McGiven said. "That I think is a big part of our identity."

Defensively, Utah has quelled fears raised last season by being one of the best teams against the run so far in 2026, holding teams to only 84 rushing yards a game. Against run-heavy Iowa State, the Utes held the Cyclones 93 yards under their 204-rushing-yards-per-game average.

If there's been anything to nitpick in Utah's excellent play during the first third of the season, it's been a couple of slow starts to the second half.

Against Utah State, the Utes failed to score on their first two drives, turning the ball over on downs and fumbling it. Against Iowa State, the Utes punted on three straight drives to open the third quarter before scoring the game-clinching touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Each of those drives took up just five plays, with only one drive getting into Iowa State territory.

"Iowa State's the one time where coming out of halftime, I thought, 'OK, we're not as clean as we need to be,'" Scalley said.

While Utah's head coach will be emphasizing a strong second-half start this Saturday, he's a long, long, long way from pushing the panic button.

"Really in my opinion, one game where you're saying, OK, probably wasn't clean enough coming out of the half. Other than that, it's not time to panic," Scalley said.

After a 5-0 start to his head coaching career, which began with a Las Vegas Bowl victory last season, Scalley needs just one more win to set the record for best start to a Ute coaching career, surpassing Jim Fassel.

Scalley and his Utes will try to make Utah history against Kansas in a late-night white out game at Rice-Eccles Stadium.

The program will be hosting its first-ever "white out" game, encouraging fans to wear white. Artist Armando Villarreal, who has worked with Utah on helmets in the past, has hand-painted each of the helmets for Saturday's game. The new helmets feature a "Utah" script with icicles, snow and mountains throughout.

The Jayhawks enter Salt Lake City at 2-2 with blowout wins over Middle Tennessee and Long Island University and losses to Missouri and Arizona State. While the Jayhawks' offensive and defensive numbers are impressive — Kansas enters the game with the nation's eighth-best rushing offense (254 yards per game) and the eighth-best total defense (244.8 yards allowed per game) — when you narrow it down to the Jayhawks' two Power Four games, the numbers slip.

In those two games, Kansas is averaging 129.5 rushing yards and allowing 348.5 total yards per game.

Even though Kansas hasn't wowed against Power Four competition yet, the Jayhawks' rushing offense could pose a threat to the Utes, who have so far done a great job against the run.

Dylan Edwards sets the tone for the Jayhawks, rushing for 296 yards and three touchdowns on 50 carries, but behind him, there's a dearth of options due to three injuries hurting depth.

Jalen Dupree has stepped up with 103 yards and two scores on 21 carries, but the Jayhawks' second rushing option is dual-threat quarterback Isaiah Marshall.

In addition to 810 yards passing for six touchdowns with three interceptions on a 54.8 completion rate, Marshall has rushed for 234 yards on 51 carries. Kansas will try and run the ball often, especially if rain showers appear during the game.

Against FBS opponents, Kansas has run the ball nearly 60% of the time — one of the highest percentages in college football this season.

Containing Marshall and Edwards will be job No. 1 for the Utes.

"Keeping a guy like that contained. You can't let a guy like that out in space. He really hurts you with his feet," defensive coordinator Colton Swan said of Marshall.

"His feet really are exemplified if he gets out in space, and so really teaching our defensive linemen how to take away his superpower, his feet, and keep a guy like that contained.That is echoed throughout our whole defense and also game plan is making sure that we can take guys like that away."

While Utah hasn't forced a ton of turnovers this season, that could change Saturday against Kansas, which has turned the ball over seven times.

"I would say we need more turnovers, honestly. I feel like we haven't had enough turnovers and just keep attacking the ball," said safety Rabbit Evans.

When Utah has the ball, the key will be another good performance from the offensive line. The hallmark of Kansas' defense has been its defensive line, led by defensive ends Leroy Harris III and David Santiago. No team has rushed for over 200 yards against Kansas this season due in large part to good performances from the defensive line and linebackers like Trey Lathan.

Harris III and Santiago will be the players to watch when Kansas is on defense. They have both graded out as some of the best defensive ends in the country and have been effective at getting after the quarterback and stopping the run.

"Their defensive front, very stout, very productive, getting TFLs," Scalley said. "They're a pretty aggressive defense. They run to the ball. You can tell they're coached really well."

Utah is favored by 15.5 points at home in what should be a rocking environment.

"It should be a pretty awesome environment for a Kansas team that is physical," Scalley said.
