articles.title: UConn vs. Temple Football: TV info, keys to the game, behind the numbers
articles.summary: The Huskies look to get back to.500 as they head to Philadelphia for Saturday’s matchup with an old regional rival.
articles.body:
UConn Huskies (2-3, FBS Independent) vs. Temple Owls (2-3, 1-1 American Athletic Conference AAC)

Location: Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia, PA

Radio: UConn Sports Network (Mike Crispino, Wayne Norman, Adam Giardino)

Fox Sports 97-9 FM (Hartford), WAVZ 1300 AM (New Haven), WGCH 1490 AM (Greenwich), WILI 1400 AM/95.3FM, (Willimantic); WICH 1310 AM/94.5 FM (Norwich-New London)

SiriusXM 270 and on the SiriusXM App 980

Odds: Temple is favored by -3.5, O/U: 54.5

Saturday's matchup will mark the 22nd meeting for the two programs. Heading into the game, the Owls own a 14-7 overall record and a 4-2 home record against Connecticut. Since leaving the conference in 2021, UConn owns a 7-5 record versus AAC opponents.

The Huskies last faced Temple in 2024, when they defeated the Owls 29-20 at Rentschler Field. On the final play of the game, cornerback Jordan Wright snagged a fumble and returned it for a 96-yard touchdown to seal the victory.

In UConn Head Coach Jason Candle's head-coaching debut at Toledo, the Rockets defeated the Owls 32-17 in the 2015 Boca Raton Bowl. This is the only time Candle has faced Temple.

"[They're] a very physical football team; a team that I think has played really good football the entire season," Candle said. "Probably 6 or 7 quarters back when they didn't play at their best, but without those, you're potentially looking at an undefeated team."

2: This is Temple's head coach K.C. Keeler's second season with the Owls.

67: UConn is 67th in the SP+ rankings in offensive efficiency after posting 499 yards with 6.7 yards per play last Saturday. Their 36.0 PPG ranks 36th in the nation.

98: Temple's defense is ranked 98th in SP+ after a staunch effort against USF.The Owls' offense is ranked 91st in SP+.

55: Temple is ranked 55th in offensive rushing success rate. RB Keveun Mason is averaging 5.3 ypc with 416 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on the season.

87: QB Ajani Sheppard led the Owls with 87 rushing yards in their 17-13 win over South Florida last weekend. Sheppard has the second-most rushing yards (234 yards) for Temple on the season.

7: After week 5, linebacker K'Von Sherman ranks No. 7 amongst linebackers in the nation in tackles. So far, Sherman has recorded 32 tackles (11 solo, 21 assisted), with three sacks.

9: Running back Cyncir Bowers is coming off a career-high 164 yards and two touchdowns. After his dominant performance, Bowers ranks No. 9 nationally in rushing yards.

In the past five weeks, opponents have attacked Connecticut's secondary. But Temple likes to run and throw the ball in short range. In their four-point triumph over South Florida, Sheppard only threw downfield twice over 20 yards in the air.

The squad mainly relies on the run game to move the chains. Against USF, the RB room accumulated 36 carries for 182 yards. By the end of the outing, Temple notched six 10-plus rushing-yard plays that led to three TDs, including a 34-yard rushing touchdown by Sheppard in the fourth quarter.

The Husky defense has been tested heavily by opponents, especially through the air. Temple may want to attack the Huskies' vulnerability here, but as a team that depends on the run, they'll look to establish there as well.

In the Huskies' overtime loss to Syracuse on Saturday, the offense stalled out in the second quarter, forcing Candle to make riskier decisions to tie the game. While the squad did rally back from a 20-point deficit twice against Syracuse, they could have made it easier on themselves with fewer unforced errors, like false starts. QB Kalieb Osborne has been productive, albeit inefficienct against Syracuse (50% completion), and has the ability to avoid sacks and keep drives alive.

"I told our offense at halftime, we're going to maybe get maybe get six possessions in the second half," Candle said. "We backed ourselves into a corner and we had to make do with our possessions."

The Huskies went for it four times on fourth down. Candle said they needed to be aggressive under those circumstances, but it has also given that group some confidence. Osborne and a balanced set of contributions from playmakers has made this offense thrive. Look for Ky Wilson to build on his first outing last week, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards, while emerging talents like Ryder Treadway and JD Willoughby look to make an impact alongside Shamar Porter with leading receiver Javon Brown out injured.

For the past five weeks, Connecticut's offensive line has consistently improved, which is one of many positives Candle took away from Saturday's battle. This has helped Bowers find the hole more easily as the Huskies mounted a more balanced offensive attack. The O-line needs to continue its improvement and try to contain the pressure on Osborne in this game.

articles.title: Las Vegas Raiders-New England Patriots FEED topic: Will wide receivers be more involved in offense?
articles.summary: Spotlight is on Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Cody White in New England
articles.body:
Wide receiver Tre Tucker is the Las Vegas Raiders' leading receiver with 15 catches for 233 yards and a touchdown heading into the Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots.

However, tight ends Brock Bowers (16/202/2) and Michael Mayer (20/169/1) and running back Ashton Jeanty (19/165/2) occupy the second through fourth spots, and no other receiver has more than 65 yards on the campaign. On top of that, the majority of Tucker's production came in one game, recording five receptions, 119 yards and his lone score in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Granted, this shouldn't be too surprising. The position is viewed as one of, if not the, weakest spots on the Raiders' roster . Also, Las Vegas was expected to have a tight end-heavy offense after hiring Klint Kubiak as head coach in the offseason, especially since Bowers is such a unique offensive weapon. However, Kubiak may have to lean on his receivers more in New England.

According to StatMuse , the Patriots have only allowed 19 catches for 104 yards and have yet to surrender a touchdown to a tight end during their first four games of the season. Last week was especially impressive since Dalton Kincaid of the Buffalo Bills came into the game leading the position in receiving yards (263) but was limited to just seven yards against the Pats.

Of course, Bowers is more than capable of bucking that trend. But regardless, the Raiders need to get more production out of their wideouts moving forward.

After Tucker, Cody White has been the team's next most productive receiver with five catches, 64 yards and a team-leading three touchdowns. As the latter number suggests, White has been a valuable red zone target with his contested-catch ability. However, he needs to be more productive between the 20s to have a bigger role in the offense moving forward.

Then, there's the guy many are pointing the finger at: Jalen Nailor. Despite signing a three-year, $35 million contract in free agency this offseason, Nailor has just five catches for 52 yards and hasn't found the end zone yet in four games with the Silver and Black. Obviously, that's not what the organization bargained for during the spring. This being said, Nailor suffered a concussion last week and has not cleared the league's protocol at the time of writing, meaning he may not play Sunday.

[Editor's note: Kubiak said that Nailor is out for the Patriots game after this was written, shifting the focus to Malik Benson and Dareke Young.]

It's still early in the season, so there's time for a wide receiver to step up and to get more production out of the position. However, the clock is ticking, and it feels like the timeline is speeding up since the surprising 3-1 Raiders are in the playoff conversation after the first quarter of the season . That's led to some trade rumors circulating in Sin City with the NFL's deadline about a month away.

Many have started to speculate that receivers like Marvin Harrison Jr., Brian Thomas Jr., Jerry Jeudy and Chris Godwin could be on general manager John Spytek's radar. So, Tucker, White and Nailor should feel some pressure heading into Sunday, especially given the Patriots' success against tight ends.

To be fair, Marcus Johnson showed on the latest Tape Don't Lie that there have been situations where wideouts have gotten open, but quarterback Kirk Cousins opted to throw elsewhere. That isn't something new for Cousins, who has built a reputation for using his check-down options in the passing game. And who could blame him, given the difference in talent between the Raiders' tight ends and wide receivers?

But that might not be the case in New England, meaning Cousins will have to rely on his receivers more than he has in the first month of the season. That creates an opportunity for Tucker, White, Nailor or any other wideout on the roster to have a big day.

So, for this week's game day discussion on The FEED , we'll be keeping tabs on Las Vegas' wide receivers. The game kicks off at 10:00 a.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin' some ball with y'all!

The Green Bay Packers are officially going to be out running back Chris Brooks (and receiver Savion Williams) against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, according to the Packers' final injury report of the week. Brooks left Week 4 action with an ankle injury and was a non-participant for all three practices this week. The team already moved up running back Pierre Strong Jr. from the practice squad to the active roster, so it's almost certain that Green Bay will roll into their divisional matchup with MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Strong as their three-man backfield.

Two players were also listed as doubtful for the game, meaning there's a good chance they'll miss Sunday's action: left guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quadricep). Both Banks and Monk were non-participants on Wednesday and Thursday, but were limited participants for Friday's practice. Thankfully, the Packers have 11 offensive linemen on the 53-man roster, so they can afford to scratch three players at the position and would still have an eight-man unit going into games.

Players listed as questionable, true toss-ups, are offensive lineman Jager Burton (back), defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle) and defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (toe). Burton and Campbell were limited participants in practice for most of the week (Burton was only a non-participant on Wednesday), while Hargrave was a full participant until Friday, when he popped up on the injury report and was listed as a limited participant.

Like the offensive line, the defensive line is "oversigned," as the team has seven at the position on the 53-man roster, while the team generally keeps five players up on the 48-man game-day roster. Because Strong and Kristian Welch (backfilling for Edgerrin Cooper at the linebacker position) have already been brought up from the practice squad, don't expect there to be moves made by the team before kickoff.

On the Bears' end of the injury report, the most notable piece of news was that quarterback Caleb Williams went from a non-participant (hamstring) on Thursday to a limited participant on Friday and was given a questionable status going into Week 5. Rule out are linebacker Keyshaun Eliott (quadricep) and running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe). Beyond Williams, three other Chicago players are questionable: cornerback Kyler Gordon (calf), linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles) and defensive lineman Shemar Turner (knee) — all of whom are on the Bears' injury lists but have had their practice windows opened up.

articles.title: Film Study: Why the Texans Defense Needs to Be More Aggressive
articles.summary: The Houston Texans defense has not lived up to their expectations so far this season. Here's what stands out about their issues from film.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans have been known for their defense over the past year. It was supposed to be a continuation of that same dominant unit for the 2026 season as well. There were some new pieces added to the group, and the expectation was that this Texans defense could be generational.

Well, so far this season, that has not been the case at all. This Texans defense has not been a top five unit, let alone a top 10 one this season. The play has been about average. Given that the whole talk about the Texans in the offseason was a team led by their incredible defense and all that was needed was average offensive play.

Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has played excellently so far this season and has honestly done all he could with the support he's gotten. When the Houston offense has been healthy, it has performed. The defense hasn't held its end of the bargain.

That was on display against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4, among other games. The late-game collapses have also been a problem against the Indianapolis Colts and Buffalo Bills. There's no doubt that the Texans defense has the talent to be just as good as last year. However, it hasn't come together through four games.

Film Study: Why the Texans Defense Needs to Be More Aggressive

When the tape is on, it's clear that the Texans are missing some opportunities to play a bit more aggressively given the kind of talent that is in the secondary. While the Texans pass rush can be better, it's the secondary that is playing quite soft.

The opponents also deserve some credit, but the Texans defense is capable of playing better. The pass rush and coverage have to work together, and there are times where it doesn't. The problem is that there are gaping holes across the field in many different situations. Given the talent that the back-end of the Texans defense has in All-Pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr., Kamari Lassiter, Jalen Pitre, Calen Bullock, and Reed Blankenship, it's surprising this has been the case.

These players need to be trusted more to make plays in physical situations and be used in the right matchups against the top receivers.

There were plenty of soft coverages that didn't work at all against the Cowboys. The Texans have personnel to play press coverage or at least guard the first downs. Not only that, but the matchups can also be better. Adjustments need to be made during the game based on what the situation is. CeeDee Lamb was tearing up the defense, and the Cowboys were just targeting him over and over.

Texans Defense Needs Strong Personnel Matchups

Putting someone like Stingley Jr. on him or, however, the opponent's best receiver is gives the Texans a better chance of winning. The defense looked completely different in the second half of Week 4.

On the game-winning play from Dak Prescott to Lamb, Pitre was on Lamb in single coverage in the slot while Stingley went for Ryan Flournoy underneath. The Texans didn't double-team Lamb either with a linebacker underneath or safety in the end zone. It was an easy pitch and catch.

Earlier in the fourth quarter on second and 18 for Dallas, the Texans had two men on tight end Jake Ferguson and just let Lamb be wide open underneath. He ended up getting the first down all by himself.

On the first drive of the second half, Lamb was left incredibly open with no one within 15 yards of him for a massive completion. Stingley was left on the other side of the field. The receivers in general were getting a large amount of cushion to operate, even going back to the first half.

An issue so far this year has also been Lassiter's play. He's the No. 2 corner, but has consistently given up big plays. He had dropped an interception against Josh Allen that would've ended the game in Week 1.

There's plenty of evidence looking back that the Texans defense is capable of being put in better positions to be successful. Coach DeMeco Ryans has now taken over play-calling duties starting this week. Defensive coordinator Matt Burke had been previously calling plays since last season, but it was clear some sort of change was needed.

articles.title: Chargers Injury Report: Quentin Johnston, Derwin Hames OUT vs. Broncos
articles.summary: The Chargers will be without Joe Alt, Derwin James, and Quentin Johnston this week against the Broncos.
articles.body:
The Chargers are going to be down even more starters on both sides of the ball in their Week Five matchup with the Broncos.

After missing last week's game in Seattle, safety Derwin James will miss his second consecutive game, leading the way for another Tony Jefferson start in his place. Right tackle Joe Alt is also among the group who will sit this week, leaving the door open for rookie Travis Burke to earn his first NFL start.

The other five players who are not suiting up this week are wide receiver Quentin Johnston, rookie receiver Brenen Thompson, offensive guard Kayode Awosika, cornerback Donte Jackson, and guard Trevor Penning.

Without Johnston and Thompson, the Chargers will look towards a limited Ladd McConkey, Tre' Harris, Derius Davis, and Marquez Valdez-Scantling to shoulder the receiving load. Tight end Charlie Kolar could also make his return to the lineup this week and is listed as questionable, which could go a ways in alleviating the pressure on the receiver room.

Joining Kolar and McConkey as questionable this week are fullback Scott Matlock, offensive guard Branson Taylor, and cornerback Rodney Shelley.

The return of Taylor up front could be huge for the Bolts. If he does not play, they would most likely be forced start four rookies at left tackle, left guard, center, and right tackle this week. Taylor returning to start at left guard would at least provide a veteran (well, second year) presence between Slaughter and presumed starter Logan Taylor on Justin Herbert's blindside.

articles.title: Swiss Darts Trophy: Former world champion Michael Smith plans on playing '100 per cent of the tournaments' in 2027 after opening win
articles.summary: Michael Smith set up a clash with Jermaine Wattimena as the Swiss Darts Trophy got underway at St Jakobshalle in Basel; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
'Bully Boy' Smith fought back from 3-1 down to beat Rob Owen, hitting 50 per cent of his doubles in just his fourth European Tour event of the season.

"I've missed this. I want to apologise and also make a promise in 2027 I will be playing 100 per cent of the tournaments. You will see me back," said the 2023 world champion.

Smith is chasing down the final spots in the European Championship race and the St Helens thrower beat Owen 6-4 to set up a meeting with Jermaine Wattimena for a place in Sunday's action.

Rob Cross was Friday's standout performer for the second event in a row, averaging 105.95 in his 6-3 success against Mario Vandenbogaerde and will take on Luke Woodhouse on the back of his brilliant opening round performance at the World Grand Prix.

Bradley Brooks also produced an excellent display of darting brilliance in his opening round contest against Niels Zonneveld, as the former World Youth Champion averaged over a ton in a 6-4 victory over the World Grand Prix quarter-finalist, in a game that saw both players average over a ton and hit 13 maximums between them.

Brooks has now won four out of a possible four round-one games in European Tour events this year, and will take on Chris Dobey for a place in the final day of action at St Jakobshalle.

Karel Sedlacek's hopes of sealing a spot at the European Championship continue into Saturday's action as he swept aside Sebastian Bialecki to stay alive in the race for place in Dortmund later this month.

The Czech star averaged upwards of a ton and came back from 4-3 down to defeat the Pole 6-4, which included a brilliant 86 checkout on the bull to break the throw for the first time in the contest.

Stefan Bellmont produced a brilliant display on home soil in Basel as he created history by becoming the third Swiss player to win a match at the tournament, as he beat Andrew Gilding 6-3.

The 37-year-old, who featured in his tenth European Tour event in his career, pinned five legs on the spin to defeat the former UK Open champion, and has his eyes set on a place in Saturday's action.

"Playing in front of your home crowd is very special and I wanted to win so much." Bellmont reflected, who managed to win only his third match on the European Tour and will face Krzysztof Ratajski in round two.

"There were quite a few nerves in the early stages of the match, but thankfully I was able to raise my game.

"I know I will have to play better tomorrow but for now I just want to enjoy this amazing moment."

Maik Kuivenhoven ended a losing streak of almost five years in Basel, as the Dutchman beat compatriot Raymond van Barneveld 6-3 to deny van Barneveld his first European Tour victory of the year.

Dave Chisnall and Tom Bissell both secured last-leg victories in their opening round contests against Alan Soutar and Joe Cullen respectively.

Cristo Reyes' first win on the European Tour since May came in style, as the Spaniard beat Scotsman Cameron Menzies with an average of 98 and will face Ryan Searle next.

The Swiss Darts Trophy continues with a bumper double session on Saturday, as the 16 seeded representatives enter the fray on Day Two in Basel.
